item.aggregated_output: # Documenting changes For a document describing changes to an interface its callers keep calling. ## Marking changes Add a line to the header: `Comparison baseline: branch {branch} compared with {base}`. - Open with what the caller must change, most disruptive first: each breaking change and the action it requires, then optional new capabilities. The rest of the document is the reference behind that list. - The operation table gains Type (added / modified / deleted / reused) and Compatibility columns, so a caller sees which rows force integration work. Classify by affected behavior, including shared dependencies; added or reused labels do not establish compatibility. - Add a one-line change summary for added or modified interfaces, such as `request +fieldA, fieldB required Y->N; response +fieldC`. - Field tables of a modified interface gain Change (added / modified / deleted / unchanged) and Compatibility columns. Compatibility carries a verdict only on changed rows; unchanged rows use `-`. - For modified fields, write `old->new` in the note, such as `required Y->N`, `Long->String`, or `enum +ENUM_VALUE`. - Deleted fields stay visible. Read their old type and description from `git show {base}:file`, mark them deleted, and note the former contract. - A fully added interface can mark the section as added without marking every field. ## Compatibility Every changed or deleted interface carries exactly one verdict — `compatible`, `breaking`, or `not-assessed` — against the supported old contract. Establish that contract from its published schema, declarations, documented guarantees, or other authoritative evidence. A counterexample that was valid under the old contract and fails under the new one establishes `breaking`, even when the actual caller inventory is unavailable. Record known consumer impact and missing consumer inventory separately; unknown impact does not erase a proven contract violation. Assess compatibility for the supported old caller talking to the new server; include the reverse direction when rollout or mixed versions require it. Compare accepted inputs, promised outputs, and observable effects, using the actual wire format. Include source/library compatibility when callers use published signatures or generated clients. Known consumer checks can demonstrate additional breaks; absence of observed usage does not retire a published guarantee. These are investigation prompts, not automatic verdicts: | Change | What must be established | | --- | --- | | Request field added | Old requests remain valid; any required value has a compatible default or negotiated version | | Request field removed | Old payloads are still accepted and dropping the value preserves promised semantics | | Response field added | Supported consumers tolerate unknown fields and the payload still satisfies the schema | | Response field removed or made nullable | Published presence/nullability guarantees remain satisfied; if a guarantee is removed, report breaking | | Type, enum, or validation changed | Old valid inputs remain accepted and new outputs remain within consumers' supported domain | | Route or operation replaced | The old entry remains supported, or report breaking and name its replacement | Assign each compatibility verdict in this order: 1. If an old-contract violation is proven, use `breaking`. 2. If all affected contract obligations are established as preserved, use `compatible`. 3. Otherwise, use `not-assessed`. Name the undecidable obligation and missing evidence. For an interface with multiple changes, any `breaking` change makes the interface `breaking`. If none is breaking but any remains unknown, use `not-assessed`. Describe the breaking interaction and migration, not just the changed declaration. # {Interface or Feature} API Documentation > Scope: {interfaces or business chain covered; N operations}. > Protocol: `{rpc|http}`. Updated: {date}. Remove the sections the scope does not need. --- ## Conventions Everything every call shares, written once from verified project conventions: + RPC: dispatch or gateway endpoint, request envelope, and response envelope. + HTTP: base URL, context path, response wrapper, and credential position. + Auth, pagination, failure handling, ID and time formats. + Examples in this document are illustrative; real IDs and values come from the caller's data. --- ## Operations | # | Interface | Operation identifier or route | Summary | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | [{name}](#{name}) | `{operation identifier}` / `{METHOD} {path}` | {summary} | When these interfaces replace older ones, add the old route beside each row. --- ## 1. {name} - {display name} + **API**: RPC -> `{operation identifier or service.method}` / HTTP -> `{METHOD} {full path}` + **Auth**: only when it differs from Conventions. + Caller-visible preconditions, ordering or idempotency, when the interface has them. **Request** ({RequestClass}) A few fields fit a list: `{field}` ({type}, required) — {meaning}. Use a table for more: | Field | Type | Required | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | {field} | {type} | required / optional / conditional / unconfirmed | {meaning; value, length or format; the condition for conditional; what to send while unconfirmed} | | {obj}.{sub} | {Type} | optional | {state when requiredness applies only if the parent is present} | | {list}[] | [{TypeName}](#{typename}) | optional | {a shared type is referenced, not expanded} | For HTTP add a Position column (path / query / header / body). ```json { "field": "value" } ``` **Response** `data` ({ResponseClass}) No payload: one line, such as "`data` is null on success". A shared type: name it and link to Types. Otherwise: | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | data.field | {Type} | {meaning; presence and nullability when the caller must handle them} | Add a response example when the shape is not obvious from the table. **Errors**: only those specific to this interface; shared handling is in Conventions. | Error code / HTTP status | Message | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | {code} | {message} | {condition} | --- Repeat the interface section until the inventory is complete. ## Types One section per type that more than one interface uses. ### {TypeName} | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | {field} | {type} | {meaning} | ## Enums If enum values come from a lookup interface, point to that interface instead of hard-coding the values here. ## Differences From The Old Interface, If Replacing One | # | Difference | Old | New | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | {what the caller must change} | {old} | {new} | ## Integration Notes, If Needed Cross-interface rules the caller follows: call order, fallback behavior, parameter priority. Add an interaction diagram only when it clarifies the caller's contract; read [DERIVED-VIEWS.md](DERIVED-VIEWS.md) before drawing one.

item.text:
已生成可交给前端的 [订单接口变更说明](/private/var/folders/8x/2zb93d5x3qx2fml_5zbv2hnr0000gn/T/organon-codex-apidiff-WcZfu9/docs/interfaces/API_Changes_2026-11-26.md)，覆盖 3 个接口。

- **创建订单**改传 `note`、改读 `data.note`。旧 `remark` 会被忽略。单项数量须为 `1–99` 的整数，超限返回 HTTP `400`、`code=40002`。
- **订单详情**改读 `data.note`，当前固定返回空字符串。
- **下单金额与物流**方面，下单新增字符串 `data.payAmount`，当前固定为 `"0.00"`。新增物流查询目前返回空物流信息。

以 `main`（`fb14a06`）和 `feature/order-v2`（`9e18371`）的代码为依据，已用本地路由函数核对 JSON 示例、数量边界和错误返回。网关行为需联调复核，新增字段对严格解码器的兼容性需在前端回归。实付金额、币种以及物流事件的字段和顺序待后端确认。
